title: Open Quantum Problem 40: the pinching inequality for word averages for all word lengths, and the status of the refined BMV lower bound
description: IQOQI Vienna Open Quantum Problem 40 (Hagele) asks whether tr(A^n B^m) >= p_{n,m}(A,B) >= tr exp(n log A + m log B) for positive matrices A, B, where p_{n,m} is the average trace of all words with n letters A and m letters B. The upper half is false (Cha and Lee, 2026). The pinching inequality p_{n,m}(A,B) >= tr(A^n E_A(B)^m), conjectured by T. H. Dinh (2026) and proved by him for m = 2, holds for all word lengths. We give a written proof, and we note that it also follows in a few lines from Corollary 1.2 of O. Heinavaara (arXiv:2310.03227v1, 2023) on higher derivatives of trace functions. Our new results are: an exact gap identity, p_{n,m}(A,B) - tr(A^n E_A(B)^m) = m(m-1) int int s^{m-2} tau^n rho(s,tau) ds dtau, with an explicit nonnegative density rho built from the roots of the pencil det(B - s - xi(A - tau)); strictness iff AB != BA; a two-sided corrected bound (exact for m = 2); sign-condition variants; a Jensen form; and the explicit form of the positive moment measure for each fixed m. The identity is a pinched two-variable form of Stahl's theorem, proved in full for arbitrary multiplicities. The lower half remains open in general. By an exact computation for each n, it also holds at (n,3) and (3,n) for n = 1..24 and n = 27, 30, ..., 60, in every dimension. We prove it when min(n,m) <= 2; at (n,m) = (3,3), (3,4), (4,3), (4,4), (4,6) and (6,4), in every dimension; when A or B has at most two distinct eigenvalues (any dimension); and when B is entrywise nonnegative in some eigenbasis of A, which covers every 2 x 2 pair. The (3,3) case, tr(A^3 B^3) + 2 Re tr(A^2 B A B^2) >= 3 tr((AB)^3), has an elementary proof by an explicit certificate, while its single-word version is false; its 2 x 2 case already follows from a theorem of Furuichi, Kuriyama and Yanagi (2009). The other five cases follow from exact rational sum-of-squares certificates, and certificates of that type provably do not exist at (3,3) and (6,3) for the substitutions tried. These new cases were checked internally with independently written code; they have not been refereed externally. We also document extensive numerical evidence and list routes that provably fail. The negative answer to OQP 40 (the Cha-Lee counterexample, also for a positive definite perturbation) and the pinching inequality for all word lengths, with its exact gap identity, are machine-checked in Lean 4 with Mathlib, using only the standard axioms, as is the (3,3) inequality tr(A^3 B^3) + 2 Re tr(A^2 B A B^2) >= 3 tr((AB)^3). The repository contains the proofs, the Lean formalization, the certificates, independent checks in exact and ball arithmetic, code and logs.
